extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians and authors considering submission to the Nagoya Mathematical Journal (potential journal contributors)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and policies for authors submitting original pure-mathematics research to the Nagoya Mathematical Journal, including scope, submission system requirements, and open-access options. The page describes the journal's aims (high-quality, general-interest pure mathematics) and procedural notes for submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original research of the highest quality
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal has endeavoured to publish original research papers of the highest quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Nagoya Mathematical Journal was founded to publish original research papers of the highest quality; submissions should therefore present original mathematical results and meet high standards of correctness, novelty, and exposition. (Page states: "endeavoured to publish original research papers of the highest quality")

rubrics_metrics.name: General interest to the mathematical community
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers should be of general interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions are expected to be of broad interest within pure mathematics rather than extremely narrow or purely technical results with no wider relevance. (Page phrase: "original research papers of the highest quality and of general interest")

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject scope — pure mathematics, broad range
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal covers a broad range of pure mathematics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should ensure their work falls within the remit of pure mathematics and is appropriate for the journal's broad scope. (Page: "covering a broad range of pure mathematics")

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the partner submission system and have an account
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts must be submitted via the journal's partner secure submission system; an account for that submission system is required and is separate from the Cambridge Core account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page instructs: "You will need an account for the submission system, which is separate to your Cambridge Core account. For login and submission support, please visit the submission and support pages." Authors should proceed to the external submission system to upload manuscripts and follow its procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow the journal's author instructions / preparing your materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should review the journal's author instructions, especially the 'preparing your materials' page, before submitting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page explicitly requests: "Please review this journal's author instructions, particularly the preparing your materials page, before submitting your manuscript." This implies requirements on file formats, metadata, LaTeX/template usage, figure formats, cover letter, and any other preparation steps detailed on that author-instructions page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open access policy and APC/waiver options (from 2 October 2025)
rubrics_metrics.description: All articles accepted from 2 October 2025 will be open access under a Creative Commons licence, with multiple options for covering APCs including institutional agreements, third-party funding, or waivers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page states: "all articles accepted for publication in the Nagoya Mathematical Journal from 2 October 2025 will be ‘open access’; published with a Creative Commons licence and freely available to read online... the costs of open access publication will be covered through agreements between the publisher and the author’s institution, payment of APCs for those with third-party funding, or else waived entirely, ensuring every author can publish... Please see the journal's Open Access Options page for instructions on how to request an APC waiver. See this FAQ for more information." Authors should consult the Open Access Options and FAQ pages for license choices, APC amounts (if any), and waiver request procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodic publication frequency
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors can expect issues to be issued four times per year; this is informational rather than a submission criterion but may affect timing of publication. (Page: "The Nagoya Mathematical Journal is published quarterly.")
